title: A new life, and old lives
body:
I finally finished my paper, submitted two hours ago haha. Always a grind, the last week, I'm noticing. Proud to have done so. 

I also have been doing orientation the past few days. Last week, the first & second day of orientation were pretty freaking bad lol. It was like a birthday party for all the masters students. I've been dying to meet some fellow Ph.D students, and nope, didn't get the chance to when masters students outnumber us like 50:1 here. A gigantic waste of time, sat through 3 hours of advertisements.

This week should be better. Today, I had my first Ph.D only orientation and actually got to talk to people. I tried my best to be social, and I was quite social, though by the end of it, I was quite drained. 3 more days of this, hopefully I can make a few friends. 

Today, talking to people, hearing about how life will be, how it can be, I really bought into the jungle juice. Walked away feeling pretty upbeat. And I should be upbeat. 

I also played soccer on Saturday. Fun, quite fun. Although I saw somebody get injured quite badly, was a little scary. 

Now that I guess, the busyness of finishing the paper is gone, I'll need to do more orientation stuff, and then school. I'm settling in quite good, I think. Been cooking, making ice cream, etc. 

Honestly, it feels like I've lived another lifetime since, idk, maybe two lifetimes, since summer, since graduation. All in, what, four months? five months? I was scrolling through my old pictures of this summer. Had a nice photo of the 长江 boat tour, and I was like. Wow. I remember that. Taking those photos. Putting shades on, gazing at the beautiful landscapes. Listening to let down by radiohead on repeat. The elderly, the kids, the families all enjoying themselves besides me, and me, sitting there, just staring at the water. Pondering. 

That feels like another lifetime ago. 

Yeah I mean, I don't know where I'm going with this.

title: The Right Way
body:
Ah, what a week. What a few days. I've done basically nothing, except walk around, and shop. And then stay at home, and browse online shopping. It's just shopping. Spent so much money. Don't get me started on what I just bought and how much it was (you don't want to know). 

I've also been finishing up my paper. Been hard at work on that, grinding. I also went back to Boston for two days to help Jaden move in. Was fun. Everytime we hangout, we get into some sort of debacle. This time it was the hour spent moving mattress from the basement. Don't get me started on that, and whose basement it was. 

I also saw Jason the other day. Pretty fun talking to him. But other than that, I've been alone, just shopping. I am now, eagerly awaiting orientation, and school to start. But school doesn't start until another two weeks! Did not realize that, FDOC is after labor day. Just checked today. Now I'm like, what am I going to do for another two weeks? Fortunately orientation is next week, so we'll see. 

Really feel like peter parker. Mostly alone in a big new city. It's not been bad, but yeah, I need to keep busy.

Am I arrogant to say that I have lived my life almost exactly according to the way I have wanted to live it? In terms of everything I can control. I feel like most people don't. I was also told a while ago that I was a unicorn, that I was mostly morally consistent, and most people were not. Seems somewhat related. Some rules for me. Do no (unjust) harm to those I care about. I think I've held to that pretty well. Do good for those you care about. That may be a new one now, and a modified one. It may just be: Do good. What else? Modesty? I don't know. But I think that my 18 year old self, my 14 year old self, my 10 year old self would be happy to see the person I am. I am perhaps arrogant, perhaps not self seeing, to say that I have lived my life to a close maximum to the right way, herein defined by myself. 

Good things are coming. They already have. Karma? Or my (mostly) indominatable belief that everything will work out. I just need to keep living the right way. I am mostly sure that the new semester, this new life, will do me good, thus: I am waiting with bated breath.

title: NYC
body:
I'm in NYC now. Wow. What a time, since I last updated. Recap: My last week in Shanghai, I bought a bunch of stuff to bring back haha. Tea, Tea Powder, rackets, etc. Played soccer. Met with a few last people. Had fun, drank as much chagee as possible. Then, I was due to fly to Cali, so I pulled an all-nighter the night before my flight. Only for it to be delayed a day due to the typhoon in shanghai, only sent out the announcement at like 8 AM. So I ended up sleeping an entire day, feeling terrible, and then pulled another all nighter for the flight. Spent half a day and a night in SD, and then went to boston, feeling really, really tired. Saw some friends for a couple hours in boston, picked up all my stuff. Then drove to NYC. And moved in. And that was so tiring. And now I'm here. 

Think I can finally start settling in now. I've got my AC, my bed, and my shower situation good now, so I'm chilling. Need to get my food situation sorted, on trader joes frozen meals and $40 NYC food for now, spending soooo much money. I finally bought my dream viking pureglide pro pan set. For only $400, banging deal, but it's arriving next week. So yeah, just chilling. And exploring the city. NYC is pretty nice. I really am getting the feeling, of how blessed I am to be here. 

Thinking about the future, just a bit. It's really looking good for me. But the higher I go, the further I go, I feel I'm drifting further, letting go more. And that scares me a little.

title: Come on come on come on...
body:
oh yeah? Steve Lacy. What a song. Writing this while listening to it on repeat. It's the first upbeat song I've liked in a while now, perhaps a sign of things to change. The other past few days, I was listening to 落雁 by 宋东野, a lot more slow and introspective, but I really liked the trumpet parts and chill vibes. I listened to that for like 3 days straight, before I watched a spiderman reel with this song, and now it's this. 

Speaking of spiderman, a pretty good movie. I watched it last week, and yeah. It really felt like it captured the essence of "spiderman" if that makes sense. Of peter parker. It made me pretty emotional at some points, which I didn't expect. Thought it'd be a typical MCU movie that they've been pumping out, but no, it was first and foremost a spiderman movie. Solid 8.9/10. Not higher because it perfectly captured spiderman, but movie wise, there was still some room for improvement. 

Ah, also I'm still here in Shanghai. Hahaha, moved my flight. I realized that if I had gone back earlier, my summer would've been over. At least in my head. This way, I get an extra week. Going back 8/9, this sunday instead. Been playing soccer, but both times last week, I over-exerted myself during the day too much, so I ended up playing way too tired. And I ended up twisting my ankle pretty bad. Hopefully it'll be good enough to play this week. Really hoping to focus on fitness, soccer, in this new chapter of my life.

title: Summer is almost over
body:
Well, what I said would happen happened. I saw Ryan a couple more times. Then I saw Jaden for 4 days, with Ryan as well. we watched the world cup, which absolutely killed my sleep schedule. Played COD zombies till 3 am, then watched the worst final I've ever watched, slept at 7 am. And now they are gone, and I'm grinding my paper. Although the deadline was pushed, still a grind. And, I'll be seeing other friends now. Playing a lot of soccer. Preparing to fly back to the US. Buying things, moving things. 

Ah. I don't want to go back to the us, haha. Especially SD. Thinking of moving my flight back, I probably will. Already thinking of packing stuff. Been thinking of packing all my stuff, my bike (foldable) the past few days, and buying a ton of stuff as well. Should I buy a vacuum here?

title: Flying
body:
Ah. Honestly, not really been keeping track of what I've been doing this past weekish. Been playing a good amount of soccer, but also injured my ankle. Been getting accupuncture. Been researching stuff. Been window shopping. Finally got a gym membership the other day! So this month will probably be my fitness arc. Been seeing friends. Yeah.. 

Time is really flying by. I feel like the summer is slipping through my fingers. It's like I'm in the moment, where I am so free, but at the same time, already missing this, knowing that I will miss this feeling. 

I've also realized that I am becoming an adult now. Yippee! I don't know when the transition started. Is it a change in mindset? Or circumstance? I don't know either. Regardless, I think I've spent the past few months ruminating so much that I didn't notice my youth leaving me. 

Of course, I am still very young. Especially compared to the uncs that I play soccer with. But, I hope that I retain some of my kiddish charm. I have felt it leaving me, bit by bit. Maybe it will come back. I still remember in middle school, thinking of those dudes who acted all cool and mighty and mature and whatever, looking down on us screaming and happy kids, and thinking, "Who is in a rush to grow up? Being a kid is fun, they're the ones who are lame". I lost that screaming, that lack of inhibition a long time ago. But the other aspects, I fear I am losing too. Youth.

But, if I chunk the next few weeks, it really will fly by. Next few days, I'm seeing my friend Ryan another couple times. Then, next week, I'll see my friend Jaden for a long time. And, I'll be watching the world cup, killing my sleep schedule. Then, for the next 2 weeks after that, they're both gone, but I'll be seeing other friends during that time as well. A week a friend, maybe a little more. And, for those 2 weeks, I know I'll be grinding my paper. And then I'll be back to the US. I'll spend around a week in California. And then I'll be off to NY. It will take me around a week to get settled in NY, and then I have another week to coast. Sort things out, before orientation starts. OK, I know that two weeks before orientation is a lot, but honestly, don't have much else to do. We'll see. And yeah. That will be the rest of my summer. 6 more weeks. Those weeks will fly by like the past months have, and by the end of it, hopefully I will be ready for life.

title: Busyness - Business
body:
Wow, am I busy nowadays! Well, I have two meetings tomorrow, so it makes sense. And, also just doing other things that are occupying me. At times like this, I think of how blessed I am to be busy. To have the time to do work.

That may be the thought of a corporate NPC. Worker ant. And, this is also my last summer as well. Maybe I should be relaxing, literally doing nothing. But I am happy to have stuff to do. Not much pressure to do these things either, but yes, I think I have always been the type to be more happy to have stuff to do. Get bored easily. 

Currently sitting in a tea shop typing this up, having spent the past 2 hours sorting files. What a day. Back to work now.

title: For the sake of writing
body:
Just returned from my grand trip. I think I was half expecting to have some great epiphany while traveling, and that when I returned, I would be a changed person. But a while ago, I realized that wasn't really going to happen.

Not much to write about. Was fun. Saw lots of beautiful things. Encountered some interesting company. Overall, I feel tired, mostly glad to be back in Shanghai. 

I guess, one thing I mentioned was feeling more at peace. And now that I'm back in a familiar environment, I think that will be something I will need to actively work on as well. Letting go of minor momentary irritation has been almost, involuntary, natural. But letting go of any types of old wounds and bitterness, especially if they pop up right into your face - That will be much more difficult, and a true test of where this monk mentality may lead me.

title: More on Control and Irritability
body:
I think I have reached a good conclusion. That control and irritability can be separated. I don't want to be a pushover, but that doesn't mean I have to see things as annoying to take action on them. For example, if somebody does something to negatively impact me, I hope to reach the point where I simply take action, without feeling absolutely irritated.

Action does not need to be caused by irritation. It can simply be: This negatively impacts me, thus I will do this to avoid/change it. Notice how irritation is nowhere to be found.

I hope to achieve this, even for my closest relationships. Although, I also do fear, that with the elimination of such tempers, it may indirectly cause more detachment. Will have to be careful.

title: Taiwanese elders
body:
For context, I've been on a cruise up the 长江to重庆. It's been nice, but also, wasn't expecting that the cruise is 95% the elderly, haha. They say old people are the easiest to talk to, well, I didn't really talk to many, just been chilling, but I have talked to this group of four from 台南 who are in my assigned dining group. At first, when I saw I was put with the Taiwanese group, I laughed at fate. Lots of reminders: The linguistic quirks, 台语, etc.

But one of them started to strike up a conversation with me, and we've talked a little since. That is another thing I should be getting better at: making the first move. Although previously, I had reasons to just chill alone on this boat.

Yeah I mean, I just had my last dinner here, so I just asked them when they were leaving China, and then we ended up talking for half an hour about Taiwan, China, housing prices, TSMC, etc. Pleasant conversation. I think I've removed most of the thorns now. Conversation with strangers can be rewarding. I'll never see them again, don't even know their names, but I'll remember this conversation. Many people can leave a small mark when they pass your world - That is the message of a movie I watched recently.

title: Unasked tasks for those in pain
body:
I want to become proactive. But not just proactive. I think I already am quite proactive. I want to be able to consistently identify and act on small things that may make me uncomfortable. Things like recognizing somebody is having a bad day, going through something, and instead of keeping my distance, asking them if they're OK. OK, perhaps that isn't the best approach for many people. But doing something kind for them, like getting them a coffee. 

I just saw a video where the core argument was: The worst thing you can do for a person is to say: "Let me know if xxx...".Don't make it an obligation on them. Just do it. I guess it's a double whammy of both identification and action. Many people hold it in very well. Not sure how to address this, but I may have to just do what I can. And then action, the fear of awkwardness, overstepping. That is easier. Simply act. And also the question of who. Obviously my friends. But what about aquaintances? Strangers? Those I dislike? Perhaps, everybody deserves some grace when they are struggling..

title: Control and Irritability
body:
I inherited my irritability. A long time ago, I thought I could solve it by suppressing it, but then realized that was causing other problems in my life. I then tried just expressing it, but generally made sure my expression was reasonable and calm. Well, I think now, I've changed again. I feel like little by little, that it is leaving me. The things that are far away from me, strangers cutting me in line, or loudness, or whatever. I thought about it, and realized: What am I going to do about it? Well, it's obviously not worth it to try to change things like that. The only thing you can do is not let it affect yourself. And since I've come to that mentality, well, I genuinely have been unbothered. Tranquility. I feel much more at peace.

It's a more difficult journey with things closer to me. Things that I feel I can control. It really is a control thing for me: If I feel I can influence the outcome, or if it's something worth trying to change, I think I still care about it. But I think I'm on the path to tranquility, even with closer things. It seems I have learned, or am learning, that there are many things in life one cannot control. The only thing that is fully yours to control is your own response. Now I don't want to get too detached, indifferent. I hope to be able to care about things, but not let it affect me drastically. Live and move on.

title: Altruism
body:
Around two months ago, I started to donate to the homeless. I'm not sure why I wasn't before. It was a combination of inconvenience, fear of ill intent, bystanderism, and miserliness. Well, I thought about it a bit, and resolved all those reasons. Inconvenience: It doesn't really take that long. Ill intent: Probably not going to give cash, but I've been buying people meals/giving other essentials like socks. Bystanderism: I decided that to be an adult, meant to be someone who takes action. Miserliness: Well, I used to think that the 10 bucks I spent helping somebody was one less chipotle meal for myself. But, breaking it down by year instead, say if I donate once per week, around $10, then that amounts to ~$500 a year. That's not bad. A good price to pay for the soul. So, I've gone around a few times, asking dudes if they want anything from the grocery store, or chipotle, or whatever.

Honestly, I still subscribe to the view that human behavior is inherently selfish, that I myself, am selfish. So, I'm not entirely sure where my motives lie. I think it's mostly so that I can feel better about myself, so that I may be somebody I would admire. The alutrism aspect is quite secondary to me. Perhaps with action will come true motive, but I don't think that is likely for me. I guess I'll find out.

title: My white hairs
body: I just got a haircut, been overdue, last time I got it cut was the last week of march. The haircut was fine. I was just looking at myself in the mirror - I have a lot of new white hairs. Like at least 20. That's really funny.. I always get white hairs after a stressful period, a stressful semester. But never this many, usually 5-10. I guess that's just how it's been. Eye bags, eye lines, also more noticable, though I've been sleeping well. Just getting older. Living.

title: Slowing down
body: Been a busy few days, I have been showing a friend around Shanghai, going to all the tourist spots. I'm quite tired, it's been day to night just walking around. It's fun, but I am really looking forward to having a day off. I'm realizing that I prefer to just chill and slow down, especially when traveling. I think that is the goal for my trips this summer. I don't need to see everything, I just want to have a good time. I think I have changed.
